summary: Backend-only testing of new MongoDB-backed BOM cache feature (bom_cache_service.py, purchasing_plan.py db integration, /api/bom-cache/stats & /api/bom-cache/refresh, startup background refresh loop). All requested scenarios passed after ruling out a false-failure caused by backend hot-reload restarting mid-test (see note below).
critical_code_review_comments: bom_cache_service.build_tree_from_cache/refresh_stale_nodes correctly distinguish a genuine fetch failure (_FetchFailed, preserves existing cache / leaves node uncached for retry) from SAP cleanly confirming no BOM - good defensive design, confirmed via backend logs showing 'leaving uncached for retry next run' and 'keeping existing cache entry' during observed SAP tenant flakiness while testing.

POST /api/bom-cache/refresh is correctly fire-and-forget (asyncio.create_task + immediate {"triggered": true} return) - verified response time ~0.1s with 933 cached nodes, well under the 5s bar and the platform's ~60s ingress timeout concern described by main agent.

GET /api/bom-cache/stats correctly reflects growth: 897 -> 915 -> 933 cached nodes across three successive purchasing-plan generations for different months (2020-01 x3, then 2020-02), oldest/newest_checked_at timestamps update sensibly.

purchasing_plan.py correctly threads the `db` param through to bom_cache_service.build_tree_from_cache instead of calling sap_soap_client.explode_bom directly - confirmed no change to request/response shape.

NOTE (test artifact, not a product bug): first pytest run failed with connection ReadTimeouts because editing/creating my own test file under /app/backend/tests triggered the backend's hot-reload watcher mid-test-run, killing in-flight HTTP connections. Re-running without further file edits in /app/backend passed cleanly - flagging this only as a testing-methodology note, not an app defect.

success_rate.frontend: N/A - not tested this round per request scope (backend-only)

test_credentials: N/A - no app-level auth; SAP/OMS/Mongo creds used as-is from backend/.env.
seed_data_creation: None - used live SAP/OMS data. Purchasing plan for 2020-01 consistently returned 18 components / 5 categories / 1 missing BOM across 3 consecutive generations (identical every time). 2020-02 also generated successfully (new components, e.g. BP6X20/Packaging) and grew the cache further.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified: (1) 2020-01 generated 3x in a row - all runs returned identical 18 components/5 categories/1 missing_bom, each completing in ~4.9s once cache was already warm from a prior session (cache had 897 nodes at start of this round, so a true first-ever cold run wasn't observable, but stability/correctness across repeats is confirmed). (2) /bom-cache/stats grew 897->915 (after re-running 2020-01, no new parts) ->933 (after 2020-02, new parts) confirming node growth tracks new/unseen product_ids. (3) /bom-cache/refresh returns in ~0.1-0.2s consistently (fire-and-forget confirmed, previously-fixed blocking bug not reproduced). (4) Light regression: /api/bom/search, /api/bom/connection-status still return correct shapes/data; BOM Explorer and Purchasing Plan UI were not touched this round (backend-only per request scope) so were not re-tested via Playwright - main agent's note that response shapes are unchanged is consistent with what I observed in generate/status responses.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - no bugs found in the cache feature itself. The one transient pytest failure batch was self-inflicted (hot-reload restart while I was still editing the test file in the watched /app/backend directory), fully resolved by re-running without further edits.
